issues.description: Class ExcellenceLand: the problem statement declares the attribute 'excellentEnough' as a boolean and requires public getters for all attributes (expected signature: a boolean getter, e.g. public boolean isExcellentEnough() or public boolean getExcellentEnough()). In the solution implementation (ExcellenceLand.java) the getter is declared as 'public String isExcellentEnough()' and returns the strings "yes"/"no" instead of returning the boolean field. This return-type mismatch between the specification (boolean) and the solution (String) will confuse students about the correct getter signature and can cause tests that expect a boolean getter to fail.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the getter in the solution to return the attribute's declared type. Replace 'public String isExcellentEnough()' with 'public boolean isExcellentEnough()' (or 'public boolean getExcellentEnough()') and have it return the boolean field 'excellentEnough'. Update any code or tests that relied on the String "yes"/"no" representation accordingly.
